text:
Toronto arrives on a four-game win streak, fresh off a 7-2 rout at Edmonton where William Nylander reached 300 career goals. The Maple Leafs are playing without John Tavares (lower body), and in the five games since he went out Colton Sissons has taken his spot beside Nylander and McKenna, with Gavin McKenna on the first power-play unit. Calgary has won three straight, most recently 4-1 over Detroit, and Mikael Backlund is day-to-day and could return. Both teams are 4-1-0 in their last five, but neither has earned it in chances. Toronto holds 45% of the expected goals at five on five (the quality of shots, not just the count) and Calgary 47%, and Calgary's 4.6 penalties a game keep handing out power plays.

In net, Sergei Bobrovsky is projected for Toronto, at 3.3 goals saved above expected this season after a rough -13.5 last year. Devin Cooley is projected for Calgary at 1.6 this season, following a strong 17.2 across 31 games last year. Our model has the game close, 3.07 expected goals for Toronto and 2.94 for Calgary.

Matthews, one point from 800 career points, is at 37% to score and 66% for a point, level with Nylander on the goal side. Calgary's Joel Farabee has a four-game point streak. Our under-the-radar picks are Morgan Frost, a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous (2.9 expected goals in his last 10 games), and Matt Coronato, whose line creates chances and who sits at 57% for a point.
